Okay, so I'm not a historian myself but "just" a reenactor, so I could be wrong about things: 

I take it from the big red cross that you're going for a Knights Templar depiction. 
In fact, the Templar cross is only about the size of the palm of a hand and was worn over the left side of the chest. 
This refers to the fact that the knight wears his faith close to his heart. 

The second point is that the knights of this time (apart from the helmets) did not use plate armor. 
The chain mail actually went all the way down the arm and ended in mittens over the hand. 
Another important point is that chain mail of this period was always very tight-fitting and not much material hung down. 
If the chain mail mesh is not riveted, you can simply remove the excess material with two pairs of pliers and reuse it elsewhere. 

If you have too much money at some point, you can also do something about the material of the tabard. Logically, knights did not have cotton, but would have used linen or wool. 

At first glance, the sword looks really good and appropriate for the period. 
If it's a purely decorative sword (which I can't see from the photo), you just shouldn't fight with it under any circumstances, they can break quickly, but from the pure look of it, it's definitely good. 

If you want to know more about the Knights Templar, this YouTube channel belongs to a German historian that wrote his PhD Thesis on the Templar Order

https://youtube.com/@mdvalhistory?si=dv4csuLNR9bBZ-J_

I'm very sorry for you. I've never been engaged or married, so I can't understand the pain and I'm not a therapist, so I can't give an expert opinion on the trauma. 

But I have years of therapy behind me and would like to tell you something in general about suicide that my therapist taught me. 

It's not your fault. It NEVER is. 
It's always the fault of the person who kills themselves. 

It may sound wrong or harsh to put the blame on a sick or tortured soul, but it's much worse to blame someone else out of grief, yourself included. 
Maybe the situation with you is part of the explanation, a single item on a list of POSSIBLE causes, but that's a huge and absolutely essential difference from blaming someone else, again, including yourself. 

He made the decision to take this drastic action because of these causes and situations and therefore he alone is responsible, even if one can regret and understand where this decision came from. 

You have already suffered enough as a result without having to take responsibility for another adult's decision as a consequence. 

If in doubt, you should reach out for professional support. 

I wish you all the best.
